sentences.text: This appeal is filed challenging the order dated 09.09.2022 on I.A.Nos.I and II in O.S.No.1132/2022 on the file of the XXXIX Additional City Civil Judge, Bangalore City.

entities.text: Additional City Civil Judge, Bangalore City
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. This matter is listed for admission.
Heard the learned counsel appearing for the respective parties.

3. The factual matrix of the case of the appellant/plaintiff before the Trial Court is that the plaintiff has purchased site No.590 measuring east to west 60 feet and north to south 40 feet totally measuring 2400 square feet which is the plaint schedule property from the Bank Officers and Officials House Building Co-operative Society Limited under a registered sale deed dated 08.06.2006.

entities.text: Officials House Building Co-operative Society Limited
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: On the strength of the said registered sale deed, the khata of the schedule property was changed in the name of the plaintiff who is also paying the property tax to the BBMP since then.
The defendant who is claiming to be the owner of the land to an extent of 23 guntas in Sy.No.79/2A of Dodda Kallasandra village is trying to encroach upon the plaint schedule property.
The plaintiff approached the jurisdictional police who refused to receive the complaint and directed him to work out his remedy in the competent Civil Court.
Therefore, the plaintiff filed the suit for the relief of permanent injunction and I.A.No.1 is also filed seeking an order of temporary injunction for immediate restraint of the defendant.
The Trial Court considering the materials available on record granted the ex-parte order of temporary injunction which is continued till the date.
4. After service of notice, the defendant entered his appearance and filed the written statement and adopted the same as objections to I.A.No.1.

In the written statement, it is contended that he is the owner in possession of 23 guntas of land out of the larger extent in Sy.No.79/2A of Doddakallasandra village which is described as written statement schedule property.
He purchased the said 23 guntas of land under the registered sale deed dated 27.11.1980.
On the strength of the said registered sale deed, his name came to be mutated in the revenue records of Sy.No.79/2A to an extent of 23 guntas by certification of mutation entry.
Since then, he is in peaceful possession and enjoyment of the said 23 guntas of land in Sy.No.79/2A.
The land in Sy.No.79/2A of Dodda Kallasandra village originally measures 1 acre 30 guntas.
The Government has acquired 30 guntas of Sri M Devendra vs Bank Officers And Officials House ...

2 land out of 1 acre 30 guntas for the aforesaid society to form residential layout.
But, the said society is illegally trying to utilize the entire 1 acre 30 guntas of land by trespassing in the portion of 23 guntas of the defendant.
The said society has also illegally manipulated the records by interchanging the position of Sy.No.79/2A and 79/2B and sold the sites to its members.
It is admitted that numbers of lands have been acquired by the State for the society by initiating land acquisition proceedings.
But the notifications published under Sections 4(1), 6(1) and 16(1) of the Land Acquisition Act do not disclose that the entire land in Sy.No.79/2A of Dodda Kallasandra village is acquired.
The final notification is only in respect of 30 guntas in Sy.No.79/2A and not to the entire extent of land.
Even the name of this defendant is not reflected in any such notifications published under the acquisition proceedings.
It is admitted that the society filed a suit in O.S.No.8982/1999 against the defendant and others.
During the pendency of the suit, the society requested the defendant to transfer his 23 guntas of land in Sy.No.79/2A with an offer of alternative land for him.
With the said mutual understanding, the compromise petition was filed in O.S.No.8982/1999 and the said suit came to be disposed off against this defendant.
But, the society did not provide alternative land to the defendant and as a result, the defendant continued to be in possession of his 23 guntas of land without any obstructions.

Recently, the defendant took up construction work with the help of the developer under a Joint Development Agreement, at that time, the Secretary of the society along with goonda people obstructed the said construction work.
As a result, the defendant filed an injunction suit against the Secretary of the said society wherein an order of temporary injunction is granted.
Knowingfully well about this fact, the society has projected this plaintiff to file this collusive suit.
Hence, prayed the Court to reject the same.
The defendant also filed an application to vacate the interim order granted in favour of the plaintiff reiterating the grounds urged in the objection statement.

5. The Trial Court considering the contentions of both I.A.s as well as the statement of objections and written statement, I.A.No.1 filed by the plaintiff under Order XXXIX Rules 1 and 2 of CPC as well as I.A.No.2 filed by the defendant under Order XXXIX Rule 4 of CPC are allowed in part directing both the parties to maintain status quo of the schedule property i.e., site No.590 as well as the written statement schedule property i.e., 23 guntas of land in Sy.No.79/2A of Dodda Kallasandra village till final disposal of the suit.
Being aggrieved by the said order, the present appeal is filed.

6. The main contention of the learned counsel for the appellant that the Court below committed an error in granting the interim order directing to maintain status quo in respect of the suit schedule property as well as written statement schedule property.

The counsel would vehemently contend that the reasoning of the Trial Court that no document available on record to show that the plaint schedule property i.e., site No.590 of the plaintiff is located in the portion of the lands acquired and handed over the society is factually incorrect and reflects the non- application of mind to the documents placed on record.
The layout plan duly approved by the BDA is placed on record by the plaintiff.
In the layout plan, the survey numbers are also reflected.
The trial Judge has missed out the scrutiny of this document.
The very impugned order is perverse and illegal.
The defendant has not produced any material on record to show that he owned any land comprised in Sy.No.79/2A of Dodda Kallasandra village in excess of 23 guntas.
Such being the case, the trial Judge ought to have granted temporary injunction in favour of the plaintiff.
The Trial Court has committed an error in coming to the conclusion that explanation is not forthcoming from the plaintiff as to why the portion Sri M Devendra vs Bank Officers And Officials House ...

sentences.text:

3 of 23 guntas of land belonging to the defendant is not reflected in the acquisition proceeding and the same is perverse and capricious.

The counsel also vehemently contend that the material on record clearly establishes that the total extent of Sy.No.79/2A is 1 acre 30 guntas, out of that total extent,
only 30 guntas was acquired.
Admittedly, the acquired extent of 30 guntas consists of 23 guntas belonging to the defendant.
The trial Judge has lost sight of the fact that the remaining extent of land is not belonging to the defendant and the defendant has not produced any material in this regard.
The very approached of the Trial Court is erroneous.

The trial Judge failed to apply the principle that admitted fact need not be proved having regard to the categorical admission made in the written statement and the order sheet of O.S.No.8982/1999 coupled with the fact that the defendant has not produced any material on record before the Court to show that the defendant is owning the land in excess of 23 guntas in Sy.No.79/2A.

The defendant suppressing the material facts played fraud on the Court and suppressed the fact of execution of exchange deed dated 23.02.2004 under which he has taken 1 acre 35 guntas of land in lieu of compensation for 23 guntas.

The defendant also suppressed the material fact of filing of writ petition challenging the acquisition proceedings and contended before the Trial Court that the land is not acquired.
7.

The counsel at the time of the arguments brought to notice of this Court to the document of exchange deed and so also the copy of the joint memo filed before the Trial Court in O.S.No.8982/1999 and contended that defendant No.6 who is the respondent/defendant in the present suit has categorically - 10 - admitted that the plaintiff has become the owner in possession of the land to the extent of 23 guntas purchased by him from Kempaiah and others situated in Sy.No.79/2A under the acquisition proceedings.

Inspite of this admission, now he claims that the property is not acquired and the Trial Court fails to consider the document of compromise entered between the parties and also the document of exchange deed.
Hence, it requires interference.
The counsel vehemently contends that by passing an order of status quo, restrained the plaintiff to proceed with the construction.

When there is a specific admission with regard to the extent of 23 guntas of land belongs to the defendant and the plaintiff become the owner of the said land in terms of compromise entered between them and also the property to the extent of 1 acre 35 guntas was given to the defendant as an exchange,
now the defendant cannot contend that he is having title in respect of 23 guntas of land which he had acquired.
Hence, it requires interference.
Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent would vehemently contend that the total extent of land in Sy.No.79/2A is 1 acre 30 guntas.

The acquisition made by the Government in favour of the society is only to the extent of 30 guntas and the land of the defendant was not acquired and the name of the defendant is not found in the acquisition proceedings.

The counsel also submits that the defendant also purchased the property in respect of Sy.No.79/2B to the extent of 20 guntas and in respect of the said property, an exchange deed came into existence and not in respect of the suit schedule property.

Though there was a sale agreement in favour of the society in the year 1983,

4

sentences.text: there is no sale deed, but this defendant had purchased the extent of 20 guntas from the erstwhile owner and the Trial Court has taken note that when there is a serious dispute with regard to the transfer of property and acquisition, rightly passed an order of status quo.
Hence, it does not require interference.

Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the respective parties and also on perusal of the material on record, it discloses that the plaintiff has filed the suit for the relief of permanent injunction in respect of site No.590 which has been formed in the layout.

No dispute with regard to the acquisition of the property by the State Government on behalf of the society and also it is not in dispute that the defendant earlier had filed a writ petition questioning the very acquisition and the same was dismissed.

It is also not in dispute that this defendant was also a defendant in the earlier suit in O.S.No.8982/1999 and also there was a dispute with regard to the formation of site and the very claim of the defendant that taking advantage of acquiring the property to the extent of 30 guntas, they are forming the sites in respect of the property of the defendant.
In the written statement also the defendant has taken the said specific defence.

The counsel for the appellant brought to notice of this Court producing the document of exchange deed of the year 2004 wherein in preamble, all the properties are - 13 - mentioned i.e., Sy.No.69/2 which was exchanged in favour of the defendant that too through a registered document and also Sy.No.79/2A which was acquired to the extent of 30 guntas and also mentioned with regard to the total extent of Sy.No.79/2A as 1 acre 30 guntas.
The defendant also claims that he had purchased 23 guntas in Sy.No.79/2 in the year 1980.
But not disputes the fact that there was an exchange of the property in terms of the Exchange Deed.

The counsel for the plaintiff also produced the document for having paid a sum of Rs.20,00,000/- in favour of the defendant through the bank transfer and the letter is also produced before the Court to show that the amount has been paid by the bank and also the bank statement and the defendant also not disputes the same.
Hence, it is clear that there was a settlement between the parties before the Trial Court in O.S.No.8982/1999.

Apart from that this Court has to look into the document of compromise entered between the parties, that is, the Bank Officers and Officials and this defendant who is defendant No.6 in O.S.No.8982/1999 wherein it discloses that this - 14 - defendant had purchased the property to the extent of 23 guntas situated in Sy.No.79/2A of Dodda Kallasandra village.
That has been narrated in the compromise petition in paragraph 1.
It is also clearly mentioned that the same was purchased in the year 1980 itself before the acquisition.

10. It is also important to note that in paragraph 2, it is specifically agreed by this defendant who was defendant No.6 in the said suit that the plaintiff had become the owner in possession of the land to the extent of 23 guntas purchased by him from Kempaiah and others in Sy.No.79/2A under the Sri M Devendra vs Bank Officers And Officials House ...

5 acquisition proceedings.

In terms of this compromise, the defendant admitted that the Society will become the owner in possession of the land to the extent of 23 guntas purchased by him from Kempaiah and others, situated in Sy.No.79/2A under the acquisition proceedings.

In terms of the compromise, the defendant admitted that the Society become the owner in possession of the land to the extent 23 guntas of land but now he is - 15 - claiming that he is the owner in the written statement.

Once, he entered into the compromise in O.S.No.8982/1999 admitting the ownership in possession of land to the extent of 23 guntas which he had purchased, the plaintiff has become the owner and also when the society has formed the layout and the same is approved and in terms of the approved layout, the site of the plaintiff is demarcated and sold in favour of the plaintiff.
The very contention of the defendant that he is having right in respect of 23 guntas of land and the same is not part of the acquisition as contended cannot be accepted.
Said fact is not taken note by the Trial Court.

11. It is also important to note that in the said compromise, this defendant is also a party to the proceedings who categorically contended that he will not interfere with the possession of the plaintiff over the schedule 'B' property in any manner to any extent.

It is also specific that the plaintiff and defendant No.6 entered into an understanding outside the Court in respect of - 16 - schedule 'A' property bearing Sy.No.69/2 measuring 1 acre 35 guntas of Dodda Kallasandra village,
Uttarahalli hobli, Bengaluru South Taluk.
Hence, the suit was dismissed as withdrawn in terms of the settlement.

When such being the case, when the defendant was a party to the compromise petition and he admitted that the society is the owner and the said society is in possession of the property, the said fact has not been considered by the Trial Court.

The Trial Court also failed to take note of the document of exchange deed wherein also the defendant is the party to the proceedings and he took the property to the extent of 1 acre 35 guntas in Sy.No.69/2 as an alternate property.
Apart from that the document discloses that he has accepted the amount of Rs.20,00,000/- apart from the exchange deed.
The defendant admits in the compromise petition that the society becomes the owner and the society is in possession of the said property.

Under such circumstances, when the society sold the property in favour of the plaintiff by receiving sale consideration, the Trial Court ought not to have order for - 17 - maintaining status quo and ought to have granted the relief of temporary injunction in favour of the plaintiff.

Hence, the order passed by the Trial Court requires to be modified.
12.

In view of the discussions made above, I pass the following:
Sri M Devendra vs Bank Officers And Officials House ... on 1 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47602844/
6 ORDER

sentences.text: The appeal is allowed.
The application filed under Order XXXIX Rules 1 and 2 of CPC in O.S.No.1132/2022 by the plaintiff is allowed and temporary injunction is granted as sought in I.A.No.1.
The Trial Court shall not influence with the observations made by this Court while considering the matter on merits.
The Trial Court is directed to dispose off the suit within a period of one year from today.
Both the parties as well as respective counsel - 18 - are directed to cooperate with the Trial Court in disposal of the case within the stipulated period of one year.
